core.title: Pass a structured context with every logger call
core.given: Code containing a call on a logger receiver (which receivers count as loggers comes from the profile)
core.when: the call's only argument is a bare string message
core.then: Pass a structured context argument carrying the fields the line would be searched by; never pass only a bare string message.
prefer: Ask what you would filter by at 3am during an incident and put those fields in the structured context.
avoid: Bare-message log calls — greppable and nothing more, at the one moment it matters.
Attaching a token or empty context just to satisfy the check; the rule asks only that SOME context is attached and cannot judge whether the right fields were chosen.
unless: The call already passes the context argument (not flagged).
The receiver is not a logger (out of scope).
core.why: A log line's value is realised at exactly one moment: when someone is searching for it during an incident; a bare string can only be grepped, while a line carrying the identifiers you would filter by can be filtered, grouped and joined to a trace.
evidence: The stack's check for this rule reports no bare-string log finding.
verification: Flag a call on a logger receiver (the stack's logger receivers, per profile) whose sole argument is a bare string message, in any scanned code file regardless of production or test placement, and whether the call is newly written or pre-existing.
A call already passing the context argument (shape per profile) is not flagged; calls on receivers that are not loggers are out of scope.
The check verifies only that SOME context is attached; it cannot judge whether the right fields were chosen.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the stack's checker fails on every finding of this rule, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: code files written in the stack's scanned languages, with no restriction to production versus test code and no restriction to changed lines
bare-string log call (a logger call whose sole argument is a string literal)

fires: A logger call passes a single bare string message and nothing else, whether newly written or pre-existing.
A call on one of the stack's logger receivers has a string literal as its sole argument.
The stack's check for this rule reports a bare-string log finding.
doesNotFire: A logger call already passes the context argument.
The call's receiver is not one of the stack's logger receivers (out of scope).
Code in a language other than the stack's scanned languages (governed by that language's own realization of this rule).

neutralityNotes: The closed vocabulary has no logging keys, so the two facts the core genuinely needs from a stack — which receivers count as loggers (logger/log/_logger/_log/LOG) and how structured context is passed (second-argument object) — are proposed as idiom.logger_receivers and idiom.logging_context_shape. The language activation fact was neutralized to a file_kind fact whose language values come from a proposed tooling.scan_languages key: tooling.languages is documented as languages of production source only, while this rule scans all code in the stack's languages, including tests, so the all-code scan scope is represented by its own key; the rule's explicit inclusion of test code and pre-existing (not just changed) calls is stated in the neutral fact itself and in core:verification. Detector, validator and finding ids (bun_security_hygiene_detector, LOGGING-STRUCTURED-001) and the JS-vs-Python argument-shape comparison remain bunOnly per the notProfileKeys policy, with the check described generically in core:verification. Per-rule severity (2) and the strict disposition are carried in core:verification, not the profile. The rule's breadth — any in-scope logger call, new or pre-existing, production or test, no changed-line restriction — is preserved so the core is neither weaker nor stronger than the Bun rewrite.
